title: Run your first 1:1 with your manager
why_matters: AIE managers are typically technical, often the senior AIE on the team, and have strong views on what 'good calibration' looks like. Your first 1:1 is where you start learning what kind of calls they back you up on — particularly the conservative calls (saying no to an agentic refactor, holding a launch for one more eval) that AIE work is mostly about. AIEs whose first 1:1 establishes this calibration walk into their probation review knowing what they're being assessed on; those who don't are guessing.
steps: Book a recurring weekly 30-minute 1:1 if one doesn't exist. Insist on weekly; AIEs without it discover they needed it after a launch-or-don't decision.

Draft a one-page agenda. Three sections: 'what I'm noticing about the team's AI surfaces in week 1' (observations); 'questions I have about how things are decided here'; 'what would help me from you'.

Ask the calibration question: 'when I want to hold a launch because an eval isn't ready, what's the bar you'd want me to clear before making that call alone — versus checking with you first?'. The answer tells you her appetite for you holding conservative positions independently.

If your manager is the senior AIE on the team, ask one technical question you've been curious about from reading the codebase. Don't pretend to know more than you do; show the curiosity. Managers who are AIEs themselves notice the absence of curiosity faster than the presence of expertise.
success_criteria: Meeting happened, recurring slot is in both calendars, you walked out with one concrete sentence on the bar your manager wants you to clear before holding a conservative-call independently.
reflection_prompt: What surprised you in your manager's answer to the eval-bar calibration question? Two sentences.
